title: Aditi Rao Hydari Is the Only Bollywood Actor in Pirelli Calendar 2027
excerpt: The 2027 Pirelli Calendar, titled 'India, Beyond a Single Gaze', was photographed entirely in India and features nine women with ties to the country, photographed by Sølve Sundsbø and Avani Rai.
body:
• Aditi Rao Hydari is the only Bollywood actor in the 2027 Pirelli Calendar, the first edition of the publication photographed entirely in India.
  • The edition, titled 'India, Beyond a Single Gaze', features nine women with ties to India, including Freida Pinto, Padma Lakshmi, Anoushka Shankar, Rupi Kaur and Bhavitha Mandava.
  • The project was first envisioned by photographer Raghu Rai, who died in April 2026; his daughter Avani Rai completed it alongside Norwegian photographer Sølve Sundsbø.
  • The portraits were shot between May and September 2026, including at Rajasthan's Jaigarh Fort and in Ajabgarh village.

Aditi Rao Hydari has been selected for the 2027 edition of the Pirelli Calendar, becoming the only Bollywood actor in an edition dedicated exclusively to India. The calendar, published for more than six decades and stocked with actors, artists, musicians and models, has been photographed entirely in India for the first time in its history.

Hydari joins eight other women with ties to India: actors Freida Pinto and Avantika Vandanapu, musician Anoushka Shankar, poet Rupi Kaur, author and television personality Padma Lakshmi — making her second Pirelli appearance — models Lakshmi Menon and Bhavitha Mandava, and photographer Avani Rai. Bollywood Hungama reported that her inclusion makes her the sole representative from mainstream Bollywood in the edition.

A project completed after a loss

The edition was originally envisioned as a collaboration between India's Raghu Rai and Norwegian photographer Sølve Sundsbø. Rai began work on the project but died in April 2026, and his daughter Avani Rai took it forward, layering her own street photography from Delhi and Mumbai — including her father's archival images within the frame — against Sundsbø's portraits. Forbes India described the result as a boxed album of 18 photographs from each photographer.

"Flowers have such an intrinsic cultural context to India. And these images are the photographers' unique love letter to India; each unique yet co-existing with the others."

— Aditi Rao Hydari

Individuals, not symbols

India West reported that the portraits, shot at Jaigarh Fort and in Ajabgarh village, present each woman as an individual rather than a symbol of the nation. Mandava arrives fresh from becoming the first Indian woman to open Chanel's Métiers d'Art show earlier this year; Shankar appears with her sitar; Lakshmi said the calendar captures the many dimensions of Indian womanhood instead of reinforcing conventional standards of beauty.

For diaspora readers, the line-up is the point: five of the nine women built their careers substantially outside India, and the edition treats that spread — Mumbai, Delhi, Rajasthan, and the worlds its subjects work in abroad — as one portrait of India rather than competing versions of it.

Why this edition is different

Earlier Pirelli editions were organised around a single photographer's studio vision. This one splits the work: Sundsbø portrays nine women with ties to India, focusing on their personalities against the colours, light and contrasts of their settings, while Rai works in the streets of Delhi and Mumbai, composing layered frames that place her father's archival photographs inside contemporary scenes. The juxtaposition is the edition's argument — old and new India in the same frame, different realities and timelines coexisting rather than one replacing the other. For Hydari, whose career has moved between Hindi, Tamil and Telugu cinema and international fashion campaigns, the calendar adds a global editorial milestone that is specifically about Indian identity rather than despite it.
